chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd, saying:

Indeed Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Tahiri wrote to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) complaining about his uncle who worked for the Sultan, wearing his official clothes, and that the affairs of his Trusteeship were in his hands. So the Imam (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'As for the Trusteeship, you have been relieved of its matter.' The man became extremely worried and thought that it would be taken from him, so he died twenty days later.

key_terms.التَّلَبُّس: Wearing or donning, specifically referring to wearing the official garments of office
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (a.s.), referring to Imam Ali al-Ridha (a.s.)
key_terms.السُّلْطَان: The Sultan or King, referring to the ruling authority of the time
key_terms.الوَصِيَّة: The Trusteeship or Guardianship, referring to the administrative office held by the uncle
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام: Peace be upon him, an honorific used for the Imam

ai.seo_question: What was the significance of Imam Ar-Ridha's letter regarding the uncle's position in the Sultanate?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s precise knowledge of political transitions, specifically the shifting control of the Abbasid caliphate's authority. The uncle’s premature death after misinterpreting the Imam’s statement that he was 'relieved of the matter' serves as a tangible sign (*ishara*) of divine decree (*mashi'a*), reinforcing the concept of *Ghayb* (unseen knowledge) in Shia theology. It underscores the Imam’s role not just as a spiritual guide but as an observer of worldly power dynamics governed by God’s will.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-2 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd,

“Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Taheri wrote to Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) and complained about his uncle who worked for the King; wears their official clothes; and that the affairs of the (King’s) Trusteeship are in the hands of his uncle. The Imam (a.s.) wrote him back and said, ‘Regarding the issue of the (King’s) Trusteeship you have become self-sufficient and this problem will soon be solved.’ Muhammad became extremely worried and thought that he would be dismissed from being in charge of this affair, but he died twenty days later.”
